sources.title: Riverbend flood situation bulletin
facts: Low-lying streets in East Orchard have standing floodwater; depth and current are not surveyed.
Households should prepare for possible evacuation and monitor official radio announcements; this bulletin does not declare any route safe.
No mandatory evacuation order has been issued in this exercise bulletin as of 08:30; this is not assurance that staying is safe.
An accessible assistance request channel and reception center are being planned, but no opening time, address, capacity or transport is confirmed.

sources.title: Water network disruption and contamination precaution
facts: The East Orchard mains supply has lost pressure and is unavailable in this exercise.
Do not consume tap water or floodwater until the utility confirms safe use; possible chemical contamination has not been ruled out.
Boiling does not remove chemical contamination. Do not treat boiling or ordinary camping filters as proof of safety.
Sealed commercial drinking water is preferred. A distribution point is being arranged but its location and opening time are not confirmed.

sources.title: Power outage safety update
facts: A neighborhood power outage is ongoing; restoration time is unknown.
Stay away from fallen lines and flooded electrical equipment. Do not enter water to reach a switchboard.
Never use grills, camp stoves or generators inside homes or garages. Use battery lighting.

sources.title: Household health precautions during flooding
facts: Avoid contact with floodwater and keep children out of it; cover wounds and seek care for worsening redness, swelling or fever.
Breathing difficulty, confusion, fainting, chest pain or severe dehydration require urgent assessment through emergency services.
Keep prescribed medication, mobility aids and an asthma action plan accessible; do not change medication doses based on this exercise.
Headache, dizziness or nausea affecting multiple people can signal carbon monoxide exposure: move to fresh air if safe and call emergency services.
